book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy

chapters.file: ch37 - 34. The Lord of the Rings as Philosophy Environmental Enchantment and Resistance in Peter Jackson and J.R.R. T.md
chapters.relation: Whitmire and Henderson read Peter Jackson's LotR films as environmental philosophy, arguing they use fantasy to recover a sense of nature's wonder and model a plurality of caring, non-instrumentalizing ways of inhabiting the land (Hobbits' gardens, the Rohirrim and their horses, the Elves of Lorien, the Ents of Fangorn) against the extractive, insatiable devastation of Saruman's Isengard and Sauron's Mordor. They explicitly deploy Leopold's Land Ethic ('the conqueror role is eventually self-defeating') to condemn Saruman's clear-cutting and dam-building, and Val Plumwood's ecofeminist notion of 'backgrounding' to explain why holding trees and mountains in visual focus is itself an argument. Thoreau's Maine Woods passage on the living pine grounds their claim that a tree is more than lumber, and the film's resistance (the Ents tearing out the dam, the White Tree's bloom) is read as a call to active ecological hope.

chapters.file: ch38 - 35. Star Wars as Philosophy A Genealogy of the Force.md
chapters.relation: Eberl builds a genealogy of the Force across the Skywalker saga, using Augustine to reject the Manichaean light/dark dualism Yoda voices ('Luminous beings are we') in favor of evil as a privation of good and as 'inordinate desire' for temporal goods, which explains Anakin's fall through his refusal to let Padme die. He casts Palpatine as a Nietzschean who declares 'good is a point of view' and pursues will to power and the ubermensch, contrasting this with the Stoicism of Seneca and Yoda ('train yourself to let go of everything you fear to lose'). The sequel trilogy's disenchanted galaxy is read through Charles Taylor, and Rey and Ben's redemption shows evil defeated not by hatred but by rightly-ordered love ('Saving what we love').

chapters.file: ch39 - 36. The Godfather as Philosophy Honor, Power, Family, and Evil.md
chapters.relation: Belliotti reads The Godfather as a study of the irresolvable conflict between a nineteenth-century Sicilian value system, l'ordine della famiglia, grounded in honor and the accumulation of power within a fixed family order, and a twentieth-century American ethic of individualism and commercial success, arguing the Sicilian vision must wither in the US for lack of its sustaining conditions. He offers a four-part philosophical analysis of honor (a binding code, group affiliation, internalization, and disproportionate redress) that explains Don Vito's contempt for the assimilationist undertaker Bonasera and his willingness to risk everything (the severed horse head sent to Woltz) on a matter of principle, insisting through Michael that 'it's all personal.' He supplements this with a taxonomy of power-over as oppression, paternalism, and empowerment, and argues Don Vito's evils are morally sanitized so viewers cheer his revenge.

chapters.file: ch40 - 37. Groundhog Day as Philosophy Phil Connors Says “No” to Eternal Return.md
chapters.relation: Blessing argues that Groundhog Day, despite frequent comparisons to Nietzsche's eternal recurrence and Camus's Myth of Sisyphus, actually rejects both. Phil Connors does not say the Nietzschean 'yes' to reliving the same day (his attitude is odium fati, not amor fati), nor does he find Camusian happiness by embracing absurdity; instead he keeps changing, striving toward a better tomorrow. She reads his transformation from misanthropic hedonist on a hedonic treadmill into a kind, generous, self-actualized man as a vindication of Aristotle's virtue ethics: happiness comes from habitually doing the right thing (saving the falling boy, learning piano, serving others), pursuing objective and intrinsic goods rather than mere meaning-subjectivism, so redemption is not 'looking at things differently' but becoming a better person.

chapters.file: ch41 - 38. The Big Lebowski Nihilism, Masculinity, and Abiding Virtue.md
chapters.relation: Fosl argues that The Big Lebowski critiques traditional masculine ideals (soldier, tycoon, detective, patriarch) and offers in The Dude an alternative 'abiding' virtue rooted in Epicurean contented poverty and ataraxia (his simple pleasures, White Russians, and indifference to property), Aristotelian civic friendship or philia with Walter and Donny that holds a divided polity together, and a Wittgenstein/Aristotle-informed flexibility about applying rules that positions The Dude at a mean between Walter's rigid absolutism and the nihilists' deficiency. Most centrally the film confronts Nietzschean European nihilism ('God is dead'); The Dude answers it as a halfway Ubermensch through comedy, friendship, and Kierkegaardian and Camusian existential repetition (bowling as rolling the rock, Sisyphus made meaningful), abiding and reproducing his form of life against despair, death, and disillusionment.

chapters.file: ch42 - 39. Harry Potter as Philosophy Five Types of Friendship.md
chapters.relation: Okapal uses the Harry Potter films to expand Aristotle's theory of philia (friendship/love), which recognizes friendships for virtue, pleasure, and utility grounded in other-regarding concern, intimacy, choice, and a surrounding community. He argues the films show that friendships for pleasure and utility each come in beneficent and maleficent forms distinguished by whether motivations are other-regarding or purely self-regarding: the Quidditch team and the Harry-Ginny romance are beneficent pleasure-friendships (Ginny hides the Prince's book out of concern for Harry), while the Hermione-McLaggen date and Ron-Lavender fling are maleficent and short-lived. Slughorn's Slug Club is a beneficent utility-friendship of mutual advantage one may freely leave, whereas Voldemort's Death Eaters are maleficent, with all benefit flowing one way and no exit, yielding five types of friendship and locating Gryffindor's courage, inclusiveness, and loyalty as the ground of virtuous friendship.

chapters.file: ch43 - 40. Deadpool as Philosophy Using Humor to Rebel Against the System.md
chapters.relation: Brake argues that Deadpool advances an implicit thesis about humor as a threefold vehicle of liberation, testing it against Horkheimer and Adorno's Frankfurt School charge that the culture industry produces interchangeable, aesthetically impoverished pop-culture 'trash' (the formulaic MCU) that pacifies workers, and Marcuse's warning that revolutionary material gets absorbed as just another commodity. Following Kathryn Tanner's rejoinder that consumers can creatively repurpose pop culture, he shows Wade Wilson's self-mocking, fourth-wall-breaking humor achieving personal liberation from tragedy (invoking Freud on humor as the ego's assertion of invulnerability), liberation from the oppressive Mutant Factory by exposing Ajax/Francis's vulnerability and asserting his own autonomy, and a partial liberation from superhero genre tropes, while conceding humor's reactionary tendency to reinforce the status quo since Deadpool ultimately reproduces the genre and hands Disney its money.

holes.name: Honor and Honor Codes
holes.what: A structured moral value in which a binding code, group affiliation, internalized self-worth, and a principle of (often disproportionate) redress define an agent's standing and identity.
holes.why: Chapter 39's entire philosophical analysis of The Godfather turns on a four-part account of personal honor as Don Vito's signature virtue, which no existing taxonomy concept (virtue-ethics, moral-psychology) captures specifically.

holes.name: F.W.J. Schelling
holes.what: A German Idealist who held that all reality manifests a will, and that the 'ground' of creative order is an ineradicable potential for disorder and a dark, passionate will that must be acknowledged rather than eliminated.
holes.why: Chapter 38 uses Schelling substantively to explain the ever-presence of the Force's dark side and why rightly-ordered love (not the elimination of darkness) achieves true balance for Rey and Ben; no German Idealist in the taxonomy covers this.

holes.name: Philosophy of Humor and Laughter
holes.what: The philosophical study of humor and laughter as morally, existentially, and politically significant, including its liberating capacity for self-transcendence and resistance to oppression versus its reactionary reinforcement of the status quo.
holes.why: Chapter 43's central argument is that humor itself is a threefold tool of liberation (drawing on Critchley, Amir, Bussie, Eagleton), a distinct topic the taxonomy lacks; Freud's death-drive/unconscious slugs do not fit his essay on humor.
